title: Shadow of the Beast
subtitle: Aarbron's journey returns in a new form

body: Shadow of the Beast is Heavy Spectrum's PlayStation 4 reimagining of the 1989 game, released on 17 May 2016. Aarbron, transformed into a monstrous servant, moves through an alien world shaped by the power that corrupted him. Side-on exploration connects platforming, puzzles and close combat, while three-dimensional scenery preserves the layered landscapes associated with the original. The remake develops its own fighting system rather than reproducing every earlier interaction. The player reads the enemies gathering around Aarbron and chooses how to break their formation before another attack closes the available space.

Counterattacks and combinations give the player ways to deal with approaching opponents, while shield-bearing enemies require a change of position before they can be struck effectively. Traps and environmental puzzles interrupt the fighting with other uses for movement and observation. The health bar makes repeated mistakes consequential, encouraging a more deliberate reading of each group. Success depends on selecting the appropriate response rather than repeating one attack against every target. That emphasis gives Aarbron's physical strength a controlled rhythm, as the player alternates between recognising an opening and exploiting it.

Ian Livingstone composed the score, and the original Shadow of the Beast is included as an unlockable extra, with an optional infinite-lives mode making it easier to explore. This places the new interpretation beside the work that inspired it without requiring the two to use identical systems. The remake's detailed landscapes recall the importance of visual atmosphere to the Amiga release, while the expanded combat establishes a different playable structure. It is a return built around the memory of a striking world, giving that world a new action game for another console generation.
